For the app to work, please grant the following permissions:

1) Block: Standard blocking words are active by default. You can disable any word or add your own.
2) Focus Mode: When Focus Mode is on, all notifications are silenced and archived. Exempt apps are not affected by Focus Mode and appear normally.
3) Exempt: Notifications from the selected app are never blocked, not by filters or by Focus Mode.
4) Emoji Block: Blocks all notifications that contain emojis. For apps where you do not want emoji notifications blocked, use the Allow emojis option in the app detail.
5) Archive: Keeps your notification history for the last 7 days.
6) Allow Words: Notifications containing the words you add here will never be blocked.
7) Sign in with Google: Used to protect your notification history even if you clear cookies or reinstall the app. Signing in with Google is optional.

NO is a reliable, smart filtering app that sorts out the notifications you don\'t need. It keeps your notification tray clean, organized, and focused on what matters to you.
Automatically block spam categories like marketing, credit offers, and news with one tap. You can also add your own keywords to fully customize the filter.
Silence every notification with one tap whenever you need to concentrate. Nothing gets lost, everything is safely kept in the archive for you to review anytime.
See the breakdown of active and blocked notifications.

NO sends its own notifications so it can archive blocked ones and show you important alerts. Granting this permission is required for the app to work properly.

To filter notifications from other apps, you must enable NO in the system Notification Access settings. You may see a warning like "This app can read all your notifications"; this is a standard Android security warning shown to every user and is not dangerous.

When you first install the app, the built-in keyword categories (Marketing, Credit, Games, News and General spam) are turned off. Open them from the Block screen. Each category can be toggled on or off, and you can add or remove your own words. When a notification arrives, NO checks the notification channel ID and the full message text against the active keyword lists. If it finds a match, the notification is silenced and moved to the Archive instead of showing on top of the screen.

Focus Mode is turned on and off from the main Dashboard switch. While it is active, every incoming notification is redirected to the Archive without making a sound or vibration, no matter which app or channel it comes from. This keeps you focused and you can still review the full history later inside the app.

Tap any app in the Apps screen to open its detail sheet. Turn on "Allow notifications" for apps whose notifications must always reach you. When enabled, NO will not block any notification from that app, not by standard filters, not by custom block words, and not even by Focus Mode. This is recommended for banking, messaging, delivery and authentication apps.

When Emoji Block is enabled, any notification that is only emojis or contains a heavy amount of emojis will be blocked automatically. If you want emoji notifications from a specific app, open the app detail and turn on "Allow emojis". That app will then bypass the emoji filter.

Blocked and Focus-Mode notifications are kept in the Archive tab for 7 days. You can see the app name, the exact time it arrived and the reason it was filtered. The Archive is automatically cleaned after 7 days so it never takes up too much storage.

Words you add to "Allow Words" in the Block screen have the highest priority. If a notification contains one of these words, it will never be blocked, no matter how spam-like the rest of the message looks. Add words like "order", "shipment" or "verification" so that important messages always get through.

Signing in with Google is completely optional. When you sign in, your notification history and settings are backed up to the cloud end-to-end encrypted. If you change phones, reinstall the app or clear data, you can sign back in and restore everything. The app also works locally without signing in.

For NO to work correctly, please grant notification access, disable battery optimization or allow background usage, accept the restricted settings dialog, and disable manufacturer-specific auto-start or background restrictions. This lets NO restart automatically after your phone reboots.
FAQ: Why are my notifications not being blocked?

The most common reasons are: notification access is not granted, battery optimization is killing the app in the background, the app is on the Exempt list, or the notification contains a word in your Allow Words list. Some manufacturer interfaces (Xiaomi, Samsung, Oppo, etc.) are extra aggressive; check battery and auto-start settings manually.
FAQ: What is the difference between Focus Mode and Archive?

Focus Mode immediately silences all incoming notifications and sends them to the Archive to protect your attention. The Archive is the history area where both blocked and Focus Mode notifications are stored for 7 days. You can open the Archive and see why each notification was filtered.
FAQ: What is the difference between "Hide and save", "Allow notifications" and Allow Words?

The app has two app-level switches: "Hide and save" and "Allow notifications". "Hide and save" blocks every notification from that app and archives it when Focus Mode is OFF, so it is app-based blocking. "Allow notifications" lets that app\'s notifications reach you normally when Focus Mode is ON, so it is a true Focus Mode exemption. "Allow Words" is content-based: any notification containing one of those words is allowed, regardless of the app. They can be used together and should only be used for truly important apps or words.
FAQ: How do per-app Block and Allow words work?

When you tap an app in the Apps screen, the detail sheet lets you add "Block words" and "Allow words" that apply only to that app. They are not checked for any other app. For example, if you add "Ahmet" to WhatsApp\'s Block words, every message from Ahmet will be blocked and archived as long as the sender\'s name appears in the notification. If you add the same name to Allow words, those messages bypass every filter. It only works on text visible in the notification title or body, so if the sender\'s name is not shown in the notification it cannot be matched.
